Ang turmeric naghatag og hayag nga dalag nga kolor sa pagkaon tungod sa sulod niini nga curcumin.

copy.en:
Can a cracked turtle shell heal?

Yes, slowly! The shell is living bone, so it heals like a broken bone — that's why turtles need protection from falls or being run over.
copy.tl:
Gumagaling ba ang basag na talukab ng pagong?

Oo, pero mabagal! Buhay na buto ang talukab kaya humihilom ito parang baling buto — kaya kailangang ingatan ang pagong sa pagkahulog o pagkasagasa.
copy.bis:
Maulian ba ang buak nga talukab sa bao?

Oo, apan hinay! Buhi nga bukog ang talukab mao nga moayo kini sama sa naputol nga bukog — mao nga kinahanglang bantayan ang bao gikan sa pagkahulog o pagkaligis.

copy.en: A dragonfly has two huge eyes that cover most of its head, letting it see in almost every direction at once.
copy.tl: Ang tutubi ay may dalawang malalaking mata na halos bumabalot sa ulo nito, kaya nakakakita ito sa halos lahat ng direksyon nang sabay.
copy.bis: Ang alindahaw adunay duha ka dagkong mata nga halos motabon sa ulo niini, mao nga makakita kini sa halos tanang direksiyon dungan.

copy.en:
How can you tell a dragonfly from a damselfly?

A dragonfly's big eyes touch each other, but a damselfly's eyes sit far apart on the sides of its head.
copy.tl:
Paano makikilala ang tutubi mula sa tutubing-karayom?

Magkadikit ang malalaking mata ng tutubi, samantalang magkalayo ang mata ng tutubing-karayom sa magkabilang gilid ng ulo.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-ila sa alindahaw gikan sa kasing-kasing?

Nagkadikit ang dagkong mata sa alindahaw, samtang nagkalayo ang mata sa kasing-kasing sa duha ka kilid sa ulo.

copy.en:
What happens when two dippers work side by side?

They create a crisscross pattern! The meeting waves form spots that stay almost still, making a cool pattern you can map.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag dalawang dipper ang nagtatrabaho nang magkatabi?

Gumagawa sila ng crisscross pattern! Ang pagsasanib ng alon ay lumilikha ng mga spot na halos hindi gumagalaw, na pwede mong i-map.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung duha ka dipper ang nagtrabaho nga nagtapad?

Naghimo sila og crisscross pattern! Ang pag-uban sa balod naghimo og mga spot nga halos dili molihok, nga pwede nimo i-map.

copy.en:
How does your brain find where sound comes from?

It's a clever trick! For low rumbling sounds, your brain checks the tiny time gap between your ears. For high sounds like a whistle, it checks which ear hears it louder.
copy.tl:
Paano nahahanap ng utak kung saan galing ang tunog?

May matalinong paraan ang utak! Sa mababang tunog gaya ng dagundong, tinitingnan nito ang agwat ng oras sa dalawang tainga. Sa mataas na tunog gaya ng sipol, tinitingnan naman ang pagkakaiba sa lakas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo sa utok kon asa gikan ang tingog?

Naay maalamon nga paagi ang utok! Sa ubos nga tingog sama sa dahunog, gitan-aw niini ang gilay-on sa oras tali sa duha ka dalunggan. Sa habog nga tingog sama sa taghoy, gitan-aw ang kalainan sa kusog.

What is the Tyndall effect in a colloid?

You can see a light beam's path because particles scatter it—this is the Tyndall effect!
copy.tl:
Ano ang Tyndall effect sa isang kolloid?

Nakikita ang daan ng sinag ng ilaw dahil ikinakalat ito ng mga particle—ito ang Tyndall effect!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang Tyndall effect sa usa ka kolloid?

Makita nimo ang agianan sa sinag sa suga kay gikatag kini sa mga partikulo—kini ang Tyndall effect!

copy.en:
Is blood type AB a universal donor?

Common mistake! AB is the universal recipient, but NOT a universal donor — AB blood can only be given to other AB people, since everyone else would attack its antigens!
copy.tl:
Universal donor din ba ang blood type AB?

Karaniwang pagkakamali! Ang AB ay universal RECIPIENT, pero hindi ito universal DONOR — makakapagbigay lang ito ng dugo sa ibang type AB, dahil aatakihin ng ibang tao ang mga antigen nito!
copy.bis:
Universal donor ba usab ang blood type AB?

Komon nga sayop! Ang AB universal RECIPIENT, apan dili universal DONOR — makahatag lang kini ug dugo sa laing type AB, kay awayon sa uban ang mga antigen niini!

copy.en: In the Philippines, doctors check a pregnant woman's blood type. If she is Rh-negative and her baby is Rh-positive, she needs special care so her body doesn't attack a future baby's blood.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, sinusuri ng doktor ang blood type ng buntis. Kung siya ay Rh-negative at ang sanggol ay Rh-positive, kailangan niya ng espesyal na pangangalaga para hindi labanan ng katawan niya ang dugo ng susunod na sanggol.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, susihon sa doktor ang blood type sa mabdos. Kung siya Rh-negative ug ang bata Rh-positive, kinahanglan niya ang espesyal nga pag-atiman aron dili awayon sa iyang lawas ang dugo sa sunod nga bata.

copy.tl: Sa maraming Pilipino, ang dugong uri O at A ang mga pinakakaraniwang uri ng dugo.
copy.bis: Sa daghang Pilipino, ang dugo nga klase O ug A maoy pipila sa labing komon nga klase sa dugo.

copy.en:
How do forecasters know how strong a storm is?

They check the eyewall shape in satellite images! A clear, round eyewall wrapped around a sharp eye usually means a very powerful storm.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng mga forecaster kung gaano kalakas ang bagyo?

Tinitingnan nila ang hugis ng eyewall sa satellite images! Ang malinaw at bilog na eyewall na nakapaligid sa maliwanag na mata ay tanda ng napakalakas na bagyo.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtuki sa mga forecaster kung unsa kakusog ang bagyo?

Gitan-aw nila ang porma sa eyewall sa satellite images! Ang tin-aw ug lingin nga eyewall nga naglibot sa klaro nga mata maoy timaan sa kusog kaayo nga bagyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the eyewall is just a thin ring around the eye
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the structural feature of a typhoon's eyewall, not the typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone. It shares the typhoon topic but does not directly support the competency's skill of describing weather conditions across the storm's phases.

copy.en:
Is the eyewall as wide as the whole typhoon?

Nope! Compared to the wide storm, the eyewall is just a thin ring around the eye. But this narrow part holds the most intense power of the entire storm!
copy.tl:
Kasinglawak ba ng buong bagyo ang eyewall?

Hindi! Kumpara sa napakalawak na bagyo, ang eyewall ay isang manipis na singsing sa palibot ng mata. Pero dito nakatago ang pinakamatinding lakas ng buong bagyo!
copy.bis:
Kasilapad ba sa tibuok bagyo ang eyewall?

Dili! Kumpara sa lapad kaayo nga bagyo, ang eyewall usa ra ka nipis nga singsing palibot sa mata. Apan dinhi nagtago ang pinakagrabe nga kusog sa tibuok bagyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As air moves to the center, spinning wind is squeezed into the narrow eyewall ring!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a physical mechanism for why winds are fastest in the eyewall of a tropical cyclone. It does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone, which is the focus of G5-E-10. The content is only topically related to tropical cyclones.

copy.en:
Why are the fastest winds in the eyewall?

As air moves to the center, spinning wind is squeezed into the narrow eyewall ring! It speeds up like a skater pulling in her arms to spin faster, making the winds here the fastest.
copy.tl:
Bakit dito matatagpuan ang pinakamabilis na hangin?

Habang papalapit sa gitna, ang umiikot na hangin ay napipilitang dumaan sa makitid na singsing ng eyewall! Bumibilis ito tulad ng skater na humihigpit ang braso para umikot nang mas mabilis.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ania dinhi ang pinakapaspas nga hangin?

Samtang mopaduol sa sentro, ang naglikoliko nga hangin maipit sa gamay nga singsing sa eyewall! Mopaspas kini sama sa skater nga mohugot sa bukton aron molikoy mas paspas.

Which part of the Philippines gets hit first by typhoons from the Pacific Ocean?

The eastern Philippines, like Eastern Samar and Bicol, is usually the first to get hit by these typhoons!

Aling bahagi ng Pilipinas ang unang tinatamaan ng mga bagyo mula sa Pacific Ocean?

Ang silangang Pilipinas, tulad ng Eastern Samar at Bicol, ay karaniwang una nang tinatamaan ng mga bagyong ito!

Asang bahin sa Pilipinas ang una nga tinabrakan sa mga bagyo gikan sa Pacific Ocean?

The largest typhoon ever recorded was Typhoon Tip in 1979! It was huge, measuring about 2,220 km across.

Ang pinakamalaking bagyo na naitala ay si Bagyong Tip noong 1979! Ito ay napakalaki, umabot ng mga 2,220 km ang lapad.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga bagyo nga natala?

Ang pinakadako nga bagyo nga natala kay ang Bagyong Tip niadtong 1979! Kini dako kaayo, mga 2,220 km ang gilapdon.

Napakaliit ng virus ng COVID-19, mas maliit pa sa bacteria, kaya hindi ito makikita sa karaniwang microscope sa paaralan. Kailangan ng makapangyarihang 'electron microscope' para makita ito.

There's a vaccine, but it has limits and isn't for everyone — a doctor's advice is needed. There's still no medicine that kills the virus directly; doctors help the body fight while watching the patient and giving enough fluids.

May lunas ba sa dengue?

May bakuna na, pero may limitasyon ito at hindi para sa lahat — kailangan ng payo ng doktor. Wala pang gamot na direktang pumapatay sa virus; tinutulungan ng doktor ang katawan na lumaban habang binabantayan ang pasyente at binibigyan ng sapat na tubig.

Aduna nay bakuna, apan adunay limitasyon ug dili alang sa tanan — gikinahanglan ang tambag sa doktor. Wala pay tambal nga direktang makapatay sa virus; ang doktor motabang sa lawas nga makig-away samtang gibantayan ang pasyente ug gihatagan og igong tubig.

Parang hindi -- sa labas ng buhay na selula, parang tulog lang ang virus at wala itong magawa hangga't hindi nakakapasok sa isang host.

Ito ay virus na nagmumula sa hayop at tumatawid para makahawa sa tao — maraming pandemya, kabilang ang COVID-19, ay nagsimula sa ganitong paraan.
copy.bis:

Kini usa ka virus nga naggikan sa hayop ug mikawhat aron makatakod sa tawo — daghang pandemya, lakip ang COVID-19, nagsugod niini nga paagi.

Nganong gigamit ang lana nga adunay sakto nga viscosity sa mga makina?

Gipadanlog niini ang mga bahin sa makina aron dili sila magkuskos!

Sa maaraw na Pilipinas, ilang minuto lang ng umagang sikat ng araw sa braso at mukha ay sapat na para makagawa ng vitamin D — baka sa halip ay mapaso ka kung magtatagal.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay angay magpasidlak sa buntag aron makakuha og vitamin D?

Sa maadlaw nga Pilipinas, pipila lang ka minuto sa buntag nga sidlak sa adlaw sa imong bukton ug nawong igo na aron makahimo og vitamin D — mahimo ka hinuon mapaso kung magdugay.

Unsa gyud ang bitamina?

Ang bitamina maoy gagmayng sustansya nga gikinahanglan sa imong lawas sa gamayng gidaghanon aron molihok og maayo ug magpabiling himsog.

Ang Voyager 1! Nagtuhid kini sa lawom nga kawanangan layo sa balay!

copy.tl: Ang balahibo ng mga hayop at ibon ay tumutulong mapanatili ang init ng katawan, parang makapal na damit.
copy.bis: Ang balhibo sa mga mananap ug langgam motabang pagtipig sa init sa lawas, sama sa baga nga sinina.

copy.en: Warming up before you exercise helps protect your muscles from getting hurt!
copy.tl: Ang pag-warm-up bago mag-ehersisyo ay tumutulong protektahan ang iyong kalamnan mula sa pagkasaktan!
copy.bis: Ang pag-warm-up sa dili pa mag-ehersisyo motabang sa pagpanalipod sa imong kaunoran gikan sa kasakit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cool down slowly so your heartbeat can gently return to normal

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes heart rate returning to normal after exercise, which is a homeostatic response, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems nor mention the listed indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). assignedReviews.card_evidence: cool down slowly so your heartbeat can gently return to normal
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies a negative feedback mechanism (heart rate returning to normal) but does not explain how homeostasis is maintained through feedback mechanisms, nor does it name positive or negative feedback. It is a practical tip rather than an explanation of the mechanism.

copy.en: After exercising, cool down slowly so your heartbeat can gently return to normal.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos mag-ehersisyo, mabuting mag-cool down nang dahan-dahan para unti-unting bumalik sa normal ang tibok ng puso.
copy.bis: Human sa ehersisyo, maayo nga mag-cool down nga hinay-hinay aron ami-amihon nga mobalik sa normal ang pitik sa kasingkasing.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes warning coloration (aposematism), which is an adaptation, but the competency specifically targets mimicry or camouflage as examples. copy.en:
Why are some animals brightly colored?

Some poisonous or bad-tasting animals flash bright red, yellow, or black — a warning sign telling predators 'don't eat me!'
copy.tl:
Bakit maliwanag ang kulay ng ibang hayop?

Ang ilang lason o masamang-lasa na hayop ay may matingkad na kulay tulad ng pula, dilaw, o itim — babala sa mananakop na huwag silang kainin!
copy.bis:
Nganong hayag ang kolor sa ubang hayop?

Ang ubang makahilo o pait-og-lami nga mananap adunay hayag nga kolor sama sa pula, dalag, o itom — pasidaan sa manunukob nga dili sila kan-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each egg hatches into a larva that grows up into an adult wasp
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a wasp life cycle in a single sentence but does not use a flow chart, does not compare stages, and does not address the named example animals (butterfly, frog, chicken, human). It only shares the broad topic of animal life cycles.

copy.en: A wasp lays eggs inside the tiny cells of its nest, and each egg hatches into a larva that grows up into an adult wasp.
copy.tl: Nangingitlog ang putakti sa loob ng maliliit na selda ng pugad nito, at bawat itlog ay pinapaluwal ang uod na lumalaking putakti.
copy.bis: Ang putakti mangitlog sulod sa gagmay nga selda sa iyang salag, ug ang matag itlog mahimong ulod nga modako nga putakti.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the paper nest is used for just one year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes wasp nest abandonment and rebuilding, but does not address basic needs such as air, food, water, or shelter. It shares the living-things topic but provides no direct instructional support for identifying basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the queen builds a brand-new one next season
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the queen building a new nest, but does not describe growth, response, or reproduction as characteristics of living things. It is only tangentially related to living things and does not teach the competency.

copy.en:
Do wasps reuse their nest every year?

No — the paper nest is used for just one year. It's abandoned when the cold season comes, and the queen builds a brand-new one next season.
copy.tl:
Ginagamit pa ba ulit ang pugad ng putakti?

Hindi — ang papel na pugad ay ginagamit lang nang isang taon. Iniiwan ito sa taglamig, at gagawa ang reyna ng bagong pugad sa susunod na panahon.
copy.bis:
Gamiton pa ba pag-usab ang salag sa putakti?

Dili — ang papel nga salag gamiton lang sulod sa usa ka tuig. Biyaan kini panahon sa tugnaw, ug ang reyna motukod og bag-ong salag sa sunod nga panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it releases a special smell that calls other wasps to attack too
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not an example of mimicry or camouflage as animals changed to better suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: calls other wasps to attack too
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not head, legs, or wings used to move and gather food.

copy.en: When a wasp stings, it releases a special smell that calls other wasps to attack too — that's why disturbing a nest can be dangerous!
copy.tl: Kapag nanaksak ang putakti, naglalabas ito ng espesyal na amoy na tumatawag sa ibang putakti para lumaban din — kaya delikadong galitin ang pugad!
copy.bis: Kung manukol ang putyukan, mobuga kini og espesyal nga baho nga magtawag sa ubang putyukan aron mosulong sab — mao nga delikado ang paghasi sa salag!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its stinger is smooth and doesn't get stuck or left behind
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a stinger, an outer body part, but its role is repeated stinging, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Unlike a honeybee, a wasp can sting again and again
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wasp and honeybee but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups; the required table format is absent.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its stinger is smooth and doesn't get stuck or left behind
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The smooth stinger is an adaptation, but the card does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage.

copy.en:
Why can a wasp sting more than once?

Unlike a honeybee, a wasp can sting again and again because its stinger is smooth and doesn't get stuck or left behind.
copy.tl:
Bakit paulit-ulit makasundot ang putakti?

Hindi tulad ng pukyutan, paulit-ulit na nakakasuot ang putakti dahil makinis ang tibo nito at hindi ito naiiwan.
copy.bis:
Nganong makasundot balik-balik ang putakti?

Dili sama sa putyokan, ang putakti makasundot og balik-balik kay hamis ang iyang tusok ug dili kini mabilin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A wasp stings with the stinger on its rear, but most ants bite with their jaws and sometimes add venom too.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes outer body parts (stinger, jaws) and their actions (stinging, biting), but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of body parts to move and to gather food. copy.en: A wasp stings with the stinger on its rear, but most ants bite with their jaws and sometimes add venom too.
copy.tl: Ang putakti ay nananakit gamit ang tibo sa puwit, pero karamihan ng langgam ay kumakagat gamit ang panga, minsan may kasamang kamandag.
copy.bis: Ang putyukan manukol gamit ang tibo sa lubot, apan kadaghanan sa hulmigas mopaak gamit ang panga, usahay may hilo pa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This is equal to 100°C.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Celsius and Fahrenheit units, but it only states a boiling-point equivalence. It does not teach identifying or appropriately using units in simple science activities, such as measuring with mg, g, kg, or °C.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a boiling-point fact but does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) or use diagrams/flowcharts as required by the competency.

copy.en: On the Fahrenheit scale, water boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)! This is equal to 100°C.
copy.tl: Sa Fahrenheit scale, ang tubig ay kumukulo sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)! Ito ay katumbas ng 100°C.
copy.bis: Sa Fahrenheit scale, ang tubig magbukal sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)! Kini katumbas sa 100°C.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a specific boiling point of water at sea level but does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state (e.g., solid to liquid to gas). It is a fact about a state change, not an explanation of the process.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water boils at exactly 100 degrees Celsius when you are at sea level!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water boils at exactly 100 degrees Celsius when you are at sea level!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes. It only states a boiling point condition, without discussing heat energy or the process of boiling.

copy.en: Water boils at exactly 100 degrees Celsius when you are at sea level!
copy.tl: Ang tubig ay kumukulo sa eksaktong 100 degrees Celsius kapag nasa antas ng dagat (sea level)!
copy.bis: Ang tubig mubukal sa eksaktong 100 degrees Celsius kon naa sa lebel sa dagat (sea level)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single boiling point value but does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) nor use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a specific temperature at which water changes from liquid to gas, which is background knowledge for understanding temperature-driven state changes, but it does not describe the process of change in state.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a boiling point value, not about the difference between heat and temperature. It does not support the competency's concept.

copy.en:
How hot does water get when it boils in Fahrenheit?

In Fahrenheit, water boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!
copy.tl:
Gaano kainit ang tubig kapag kumukulo sa Fahrenheit?

Sa Fahrenheit, kumukulo ang tubig sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka init ang tubig kung magbukal sa Fahrenheit?

Sa Fahrenheit, ang tubig magbukal sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water is a great cleaner! Its molecules adhere to other surfaces and carry away water-soluble dirt.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains water's adhesive cleaning property and mentions water-soluble dirt, but it does not identify the roles of solute and solvent in a solution. No direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water is a great cleaner! Its molecules adhere to other surfaces and carry away water-soluble dirt.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of water cleaning, but it does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, nor does it classify solutions or suspensions. The mention of water-soluble dirt is only tangentially related to mixtures.

copy.en:
Why is water such a good cleaner?

Water is a great cleaner! Its molecules adhere to other surfaces and carry away water-soluble dirt. That's why rinsing with water easily removes water-soluble substances!
copy.tl:
Bakit magandang panlinis ang tubig?

Magandang panlinis ang tubig! Ang mga molekula nito ay nag-a-adhere sa ibabaw at nagdadala palayo ng water-soluble na dumi. Kaya ang pag-rinse gamit ang tubig ay nagtatanggal ng water-soluble na sangkap!
copy.bis:
Ngano maayo nga panlimpyo ang tubig?

Maayo nga panlimpyo ang tubig! Ang iyang mga molekula nag-adhere sa ibabaw ug nagdala palayo sa water-soluble nga hugaw. Mao nga ang paghugas gamit ang tubig nagtangtang sa water-soluble nga substansya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: About 97% is salty! Only 3% is freshwater
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify what proportion of the Earth's surface is covered with water as opposed to land
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the proportion of Earth's water that is freshwater versus salty water, not the proportion of Earth's surface covered by water as opposed to land. It shares the topic of water but does not provide information needed to identify surface water coverage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: About 97% is salty! Only 3% is freshwater
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires identifying local landforms and bodies of water and describing their influence on living and non-living components. The card only gives a global percentage of freshwater and does not mention local landforms, bodies of water, or environmental influence.

copy.en:
How much of Earth's water is freshwater?

About 97% is salty! Only 3% is freshwater, and most of that is locked in glaciers and polar ice.
copy.tl:
Ilang porsyento ng tubig sa Mundo ang freshwater?

Halos 97% ay maalat! Tanging 3% lamang ang freshwater, at karamihan nito ay nakaimbak sa mga glacier at polar ice.
copy.bis:
Pila ka porsyento sa tubig sa Yuta ang freshwater?

Halos 97% maalat! 3% lamang ang freshwater, ug kadaghanan niini nabutang sa mga glacier ug polar ice.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water has a very high specific heat, needing lots of energy to change temperature!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses water's high specific heat and its effect on coastal temperatures, but it does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It only uses temperature-change language without defining or contrasting heat versus temperature.

copy.en:
Why do places near the sea have milder temperatures than inland areas?

Water has a very high specific heat, needing lots of energy to change temperature! That is why coastal places like the Philippines have milder temperatures than inland areas.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas malambot ang temperatura sa mga lugar malapit sa dagat?

Ang tubig ay may napakataas na specific heat—kailangan ng maraming enerhiya para magbago ang temperatura! Kaya ang mga lugar tulad ng Pilipinas ay mas malambot.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas malumo ang temperatura sa mga lugar duol sa dagat?

Ang tubig adunay napaka-taas nga specific heat—kinahanglan og daghang enerhiya aron mabag-o ang temperatura! Mao nga ang mga lugar sama sa Pilipinas mas malumo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A water wheel rotates when flowing water fills its cups, making the wheel turn around its center stick.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and describe some ways to use movement, sound, and light to send information between two people
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water causing a wheel to move, which is an example of movement, but the competency specifically requires using movement, sound, or light to send information between two people. No information transfer is mentioned, so the card does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A water wheel rotates when flowing water fills its cups, making the wheel turn around its center stick.
copy.tl: Umiikot ang water wheel kapag pinupuno ng umaagos na tubig ang mga cups nito, kaya umiikot ang gulong sa gitnang stick.
copy.bis: Motuyok ang water wheel kon pun-on sa nag-agay nga tubig ang mga cups niini, mao nga moliko ang ligid sa tunga nga stick.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water puts out a wood fire! It cools down the fuel and keeps the air away from the flame.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how water extinguishes a wood fire, which is a fire-safety action. G4-M-5 focuses on demonstrating ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, specifically restriction of burning of waste materials and care in handling reactive materials. Extinguishing a fire is related to minimizing harm but does not directly teach the competency's stated actions (restricting burning of waste, handling reactive materials).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water puts out a wood fire! It cools down the fuel and keeps the air away from the flame.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: G3-M-6 asks students to explain that changes in materials can be harmful, such as trash disposal and burning household materials. The card explains how water stops a fire, which is a response to a harmful change, but it does not explain that burning is harmful or address the harmful effects of changes in materials. It is related to fire but not directly supporting the competency's explanation of harmful changes.

copy.en: Water puts out a wood fire! It cools down the fuel and keeps the air away from the flame.
copy.tl: Pinapatay ng tubig ang apoy sa kahoy! Pinapalamig nito ang gatong at hinaharangan ang hangin sa apoy.
copy.bis: Gipapatay sa tubig ang kalayo sa kahoy! Gipabugnaw niini ang sugnod ug gibabagan ang hangin sa kalayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The watt is named after James Watt! He was a Scottish engineer.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies James Watt as a foreign scientist but does not mention any invention. The watt is a unit of power named after him, not an invention. The competency requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s, so this card only shares the scientist's name and nationality without supporting the invention aspect.

copy.en: The watt is named after James Watt! He was a Scottish engineer.
copy.tl: Ang watt ay ipinangalan kay James Watt! Siya ay isang Scottish na inhinyero.
copy.bis: Ang watt ginganlan kang James Watt! Siya usa ka Scottish nga engineer.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We only hear frequencies from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions frequency as a term and gives a human hearing range, but it does not describe how wave properties (amplitude, frequency, wavelength, velocity) are identified or described. It provides no instruction on the scientific terms or their definitions, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What sounds can our human ears actually hear?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the range of audible frequencies, not about how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It does not explain sound production or transfer (e.g., ringing bell, hearing noises), so it only shares the broad topic of sound.

copy.en:
What sounds can our human ears actually hear?

We only hear frequencies from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz! We can't hear sounds outside this, but animals like dogs can hear much higher frequencies than us!
copy.tl:
Anong mga tunog ang kayang marinig ng ating tainga?

Nakakarinig lang tayo ng frequencies mula 20 Hz hanggang 20,000 Hz! Hindi natin naririnig ang nasa labas nito, pero ang mga hayop tulad ng aso ay nakakarinig ng mas mataas!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga tingog ang makaya madungog sa atong dalunggan?

Makadungog lang ta sa frequencies gikan 20 Hz hangtod 20,000 Hz! Dili nato madungog ang gawas niini, apan ang mga hayop sama sa iro makadungog og mas taas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: peak to peak on water, or crowded-band to crowded-band on a slinky
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how to measure wavelength in a photo using examples of water (transverse) and slinky (longitudinal) waves, but it does not identify differences or similarities between longitudinal and transverse waves. It only touches on wave types incidentally without the required comparison.

copy.en:
How do you measure wavelength in a photo?

You can measure it peak to peak on water, or crowded-band to crowded-band on a slinky!
copy.tl:
Paano susukatin ang wavelength sa larawan?

Maaari mo itong sukatin bilang peak to peak sa tubig, o crowded-band to crowded-band sa slinky!
copy.bis:
Unsayon pagsukod sa wavelength sa picture?

Pwede nimo kini sukdon as peak to peak sa tubig, o crowded-band to crowded-band sa slinky!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Moon is waxing when its lit part is growing, and waning when its lit part is shrinking!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines waxing and waning, which are terms related to moon phases, but the competency requires making drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases. The card does not address the motion, the model, or the explanation of phases; it only gives a definition of two terms.

copy.en: The Moon is waxing when its lit part is growing, and waning when its lit part is shrinking!
copy.tl: Waxing ang tawag kapag lumalaki ang liwanag ng Buwan; waning naman kapag lumiliit ito!
copy.bis: Gitawag nga waxing kung nagkadako ang hayag nga bahin sa Bulan; waning kung nagkagamay kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our exhaled air still has oxygen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses oxygen in exhaled air but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work, which is the focus of G5-L-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our exhaled air still has oxygen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen in exhaled air, a minor aspect of respiration, but does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products as required by G8-L-9.

copy.en: We don't use up all the oxygen we breathe in! Our exhaled air still has oxygen, which is why rescue breathing works.
copy.tl: Hindi natin nagagamit lahat ng oxygen na hinihinga natin! May oxygen pa rin ang hiningang palabas, kaya possible ang rescue breathing.
copy.bis: Dili naton magamit tanan nga oxygen nga atong ginaginhawa! Duna pay oxygen ang gibuga nga hangin, mao nga mahimo ang rescue breathing.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weather balloons from PAGASA rise high into the stratosphere to measure the temperature and air up there!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a weather instrument (weather balloon) and that it measures temperature and air, but it does not support the competency's action of students using weather instruments to measure and record weather characteristics during a school day. It is background information about a specific instrument used by PAGASA, not instruction on using instruments or recording data.

copy.en: Weather balloons from PAGASA rise high into the stratosphere to measure the temperature and air up there!
copy.tl: Umaakyat ang mga weather balloon ng PAGASA hanggang stratosphere para sukatin ang temperatura at hangin sa itaas!
copy.bis: Mosaka ang mga weather balloon sa PAGASA hangtod sa stratosphere aron sukdon ang temperatura ug hangin sa ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA uses weather satellites in space to take pictures of clouds and storms from above, helping them see exactly where a storm is heading!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions PAGASA and storms but does not describe weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal. It only notes that satellites help track storm direction, which is background about storm monitoring, not the warning-signal competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA uses weather satellites in space to take pictures of clouds and storms from above, helping them see exactly where a storm is heading!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a map and a record of tracking data to trace the path of typhoons that enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions satellite imagery of storms but does not involve using a map and tracking data to trace typhoon paths through the PAR. It provides general context about how storms are observed, not the specific map/tracking skill required.

copy.en: PAGASA uses weather satellites in space to take pictures of clouds and storms from above, helping them see exactly where a storm is heading!
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang PAGASA ng weather satellite sa kalawakan para kumuha ng litrato ng ulap at bagyo mula sa itaas, para makita kung saan ito patungo!
copy.bis: Naggamit ang PAGASA og weather satellite sa kawanangan para magkuha og hulagway sa panganod ug bagyo gikan sa itaas, aron makita kon asa kini paingon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Their sensors measure and send data over the internet all by themselves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sensors measuring weather data but does not teach students how to use weather instruments to measure and record characteristics during a school day. It is about automatic stations, not student-led measurement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Their sensors measure and send data over the internet all by themselves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to weather data being measured but does not identify any specific weather characteristics such as air temperature, wind speed, humidity, etc. It does not directly support identifying the basic characteristics of weather.

copy.en: Some modern weather stations are automatic—no person needed! Their sensors measure and send data over the internet all by themselves, even in far or hard-to-reach places.
copy.tl: Ang ilang modernong weather station ay awtomatik—hindi na kailangan ng tao! Ang mga sensor nito ay sumusukat at nagpapadala ng datos sa internet, kahit sa malayo o mahirap puntahang lugar.
copy.bis: Adunay modernong weather station nga awtomatik—dili na kinahanglan og tawo! Ang sensor niini magsukod ug magpadala sa datos pinaagi sa internet, bisan sa layo o lisod adtoan nga dapit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a typhoon suddenly strengthens by 55 km/h or more in 24 hours
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines rapid intensification, a specific typhoon phenomenon, but does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a typhoon suddenly strengthens by 55 km/h or more in 24 hours
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions typhoon strengthening but does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, which are the required actions of the competency.

copy.en:
What is rapid intensification in a typhoon?

When a typhoon suddenly strengthens by 55 km/h or more in 24 hours, making forecasting harder and giving people less time to prepare!
copy.tl:
Ano ang rapid intensification sa isang typhoon?

Kapag biglang lumakas ang typhoon ng 55 km/h o higit pa sa 24 oras, nagpapahirap sa pagtataya at nagpapaliit ng oras para maghanda!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang rapid intensification sa usa ka typhoon?

Kung ang typhoon kalit motunga og 55 km/h o labaw pa sa 24 oras, nagpahirap sa pagtataya ug naghatag og gamay nga oras sa pagpangandam!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists call this chemical weathering.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that slightly acidic rainwater dissolves rocks (chemical weathering), which is a process that breaks down rocks. This is background knowledge for understanding how soil forms from rocks and minerals, but the card does not explain soil formation itself or connect weathering to soil production.

copy.en:
Can rain really dissolve rock?

Surprisingly, yes! Rainwater is slightly acidic, so it slowly dissolves certain rocks like limestone. Scientists call this chemical weathering.
copy.tl:
Kayang kaya ba ng ulan na tunawin ang bato?

Oo nga! Ang ulan ay bahagyang maasim, kaya unti-unti nitong tinutunaw ang ilang bato tulad ng limestone. Tawag dito ay chemical weathering.
copy.bis:
Makaya ba sa ulan nga matunaw ang bato?

Oo gyud! Ang ulan gamay nga aslom, busa hinay-hinay niini matunaw ang pipila ka bato sama sa limestone. Kini ang chemical weathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Only the larvae (babies) of weaver ants can make silk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about a life-cycle stage (larvae) of weaver ants but does not use a flow chart to compare different stages of an animal life cycle, which is the required format and core action of the competency.

copy.en:
Which weaver ants can make silk?

Only the larvae (babies) of weaver ants can make silk — the grown-up ants can't spin silk anymore!
copy.tl:
Alin sa mga hantik ang gumagawa ng sutla?

Tanging ang mga larva (sanggol) ng hantik ang gumagawa ng sutla — hindi na kayang gumawa nito ng mga may-gulang na langgam!
copy.bis:
Hain nga hantik ang makahimo og seda?

Ang mga larva (bata) lang sa hantik ang makahimo og seda — dili na kini mahimo sa mga hamtong nga langgam!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weaverbirds mostly munch on seeds, grass grains, and small insects for food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: A diet list is not grouping animals as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weaverbirds mostly munch on seeds, grass grains, and small insects for food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: A seed-and-insect diet is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: Weaverbirds mostly munch on seeds, grass grains, and small insects for food.
copy.tl: Karaniwang kumakain ang weaverbird ng mga buto, butil ng damo, at maliliit na insekto.
copy.bis: Ang weaverbird kasagaran mokaon og mga liso, lugas sa sagbot, ug gagmayng insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a weaverbird's nest is intricately woven
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes nest-building behavior, which is not one of the three characteristics (grow, respond, reproduce) that G3-L-3 requires students to describe. Nest construction is only tangentially related to living things and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Unlike the simple cup nests of most birds, a weaverbird's nest is intricately woven — making it one of the best nest builders around!
copy.tl: Hindi tulad ng simpleng tasang pugad ng ibang ibon, masalimuot na hinabi ang pugad ng weaverbird — kaya isa ito sa pinakamagaling na tagagawa ng pugad!
copy.bis: Dili sama sa yano nga tasa nga salag sa ubang langgam, komplikado nga hinabi ang salag sa weaverbird — mao nga usa kini sa labing maayo nga maghihimo og salag!
